notes.title: What's being worked on in Core Lords?
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

A bit longer on the update than I would usually like, got covid again this month (-.-). That and my wife is very very very pregnant with our first, lots to prepare!

So outside of the usual bug fixing, optimizing and tweaking, here is what is being worked on for Core Lords: [b]A new biome and level![/b]

[h2]The Canyon[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/ab414523fae87ec684ef61495212b2f0c28b2f1f.png[/img]
A gloomy fog and and driving rain hangs over this imposing gash in the earth. Slippery rocks and ledges create a sweaty-palmed climb to a great danger. An opportunity for more environmental puzzles, battles and even new powers await!


[h2]New Enemies[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/151297cf64f49ed2b9ac3b119279292cadd66505.png[/img]
A strange corruption has descended upon the land, and the canyon and it's local inhabitants are not immune. The first of the new enemy types for canyon zone, these little guys can really overwhelm in groups!


[h2]Building a boss arena and... well the boss.[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/f9c9e2018dbace56c739086ffe6cc88d853ac4fe.png[/img]
A messy sketch of what is being worked on in terms of a boss arena and hints at what the boss could be. I really hope to develop the world through environmental story telling - any theories?


All very work-in-progress, and as usual, let me know of any feedback/ideas you have!

Cheers,
Chris

notes.title: Core Lords - Demo Update (v1.1)
notes.content:
Hi all,

A (long overdue) update to the demo has been released.

A huge list of updates, bugs fixes, QoL changes have been worked on, and I will be unable to list them all, but some major changes are as follows:

[b]GAMEPLAY/AI[/b]
[list]
[*] More enemy behavior such as strafing, keeping distance and better line of sight calculations
[*] Vastly improved AI actions and decision making (though still needs work!)
[*] Enemy drops (combat drops and permanent upgrades)
[*] Improved jumping and falling behaviour
[/list]

[b]TUTORIAL STORY[/b]
[list]
[*] A huge amount of bug fixes
[*] Clearer tutorial hints
[*] Balanced delays and pacing of tutorial information
[*] Visual and camera tweaks
[*] Fixes for puzzles
[/list]

[b]QoL[/b]
[list]
[*] Visual indication of enemy and player health and action points in combat
[*] More indicators and affordance for what actions you take will result in, especially with Core interactions
[*] Smoother movement behavior, such as better navmesh, hold-to-move and click-to-move, move-to and climb etc.
[/list]

[b]LEVEL DESIGN[/b]
[list]
[*] Better interaction with water and lava
[*] Better procedural generation for Quick Battle
[*] Gaps, holes and other kinds of collider fixes
[*] Lots of general bug fixes
[/list]

[b]ANIMATION[/b]
[list]
[*] Smoother animations, especially with running and other movement (less janky and staggered, but still working on it)
[*] New animations for the player character
[/list]

[b]UI[/b]
[list]
[*] Cleaner and more consistent design
[*] UI interaction fixes, such as toggling and buttons
[*] General visual UI improvements and fixes
[/list]

[b]VFX/SFX[/b]
[list]
[*] Improvements and adjustments to visual and sound effects, such as performance tweaks, visual clarity and consistency
[/list]


If you give the demo a go, please let me know what you think!

Cheers, 
Chris

notes.title: A bit on how Core Lords works 4# - Orange, Red, Action!
notes.content:
Hello! I hope everyone is having a good 2024 so far! An update on a more intricate combat system from Core Lords below.

[h2]How Orange, Red, Action! (ORA) Works[/h2]

Cores Lords has a turn-based combat system, but also has a minor twist on "you move I move". 

In Core Lords, Many actions such as attacking, moving and falling may have a kind of "wind up" before the action is triggered.

[b]This is called ORA, or Orange > Red > Action![/b]

Each action can be ORA or an instant effect and takes an Action Point per stage. Objects that don’t have Action Points are likely to progress a stage after each player turn ends. 

ORA can also skip the “Orange” stage, meaning the trigger will happen after only one stage of wind-up.

ORA is represented by orange or red outlines on enemies, cores and objects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/7a1dc3f911efdae53a97c9cea65041a79d2c9b5b.png[/img]
[i]We can see the enemies are at different stages in their ORA, one in "Orange" and one in "Red". Our player better move![/i]


[h3]Enemy ORA[/h3]

You can see this enemy with two stage ORA, attacking after “Red”. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/1daca0828fae1a121de6af5440611c91a4943f29.gif[/img]
[i]Above you can see the enemy used a total of 3 actions points in this sequence. It used it's 4th point to start the wind-up again, going to "Orange".[/i]


[h3]Core ORA[/h3]

Cores also can use ORA. Use this knowledge to strategize placement and moves!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/9e23edcf4a201e30a4f9786b540daa8ccfb6f12d.gif[/img]
[i]Watercores "Pop" after a certain amount of time/turns.[/i]


[h3]Puzzle ORA[/h3]

Puzzles may also have situational ORA, adding timing and planning challenges.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/7ecb473da47c37efb911cc917723ffa53ef40e4a.png[/img]
[i]The floating cores are going to drop very soon![/i]


Hopefully ORA is not too complicated! It is all fairly intuitive in game. Let me know what you think about it!

Also, as always, give the demo a go and give me some feedback for that too!

Cheers,
Chris

notes.title: A bit on how Core Lords works 3# - Core Interactions
notes.content:
Hello and Happy New Year! Back to it with an update on how the Cores interact with each other in game!

[h2]What the Cores can do[/h2]

Below we can see the basic functions of each of the Cores that you can control in Core Lords:

[b]Stonecores [/b]are, just like all Cores, part of the natural world, but their cube-like shape allows you to manipulate them. These stones can be moved, pulled, pushed, dropped and set up for a variety of uses in exploration, puzzle solving and battle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/b5b64d4457606aa8b3386a5cf0730ce0e30eb026.gif[/img]

[b]Windcores [/b]use concentrated gusts of wind to push other Cores around the environment, often to create paths and attack offensively.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/c0b31a92df5930e788b3e77c1f45abed0ebc7141.gif[/img]

[b]Watercores [/b]are controlled water sources and are used to bounce Stonecores and Flamecores in directions controlled by the player. Characters moving through Watercores are also slowed down.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/628c4bc4c189140865621a29c5800fb8eb561f80.gif[/img]

[b]Flamecores[/b] are flame and lava in a controllable form. They can be quite destructive and do more damage than Stonecores. They also leave a pool of lava where they land, acting as an dangerous obstacle for any nearby.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/2d72bb0159e328b6ba7ad2e02e0c8214074cf21a.gif[/img]


[h2]Interactions with other Cores[/h2]

What happens when two cores interact?

[b]Stonecore + Windcore[/b]
A Windcore can be formed near a Stonecore, which will push it in the direction of the facing of the Windcore.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/ac1fb170315a04d7d5db4b848d9fda3c3bcda4da.gif[/img]


[b]Stonecore + Watercore[/b]
A Stonecore will bounce in the direction of the Watercore facing when being pushed or falling into a one of more of them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/628c4bc4c189140865621a29c5800fb8eb561f80.gif[/img]


[b]Stonecore + Flamecore[/b]
A Stonecore will pop a Flamecore’s form and remove it.


[b]Windcore + Flamecore[/b]
A Flamecore can be pushed by a Windcore, the same as a Windcore and Stonecore interaction.


[b]Windcore + Watercore[/b]
We cannot push a Watercore, as the form of the Watercore is too fragile when moving.


[b]Watercore + Flamecore[/b]
A Flamecore coming into contact with a Watercore will have the unique effect of cooling off the lava and flame, creating a new Stonecore.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/9158bcf45308399f125151074e0796da5fb55129.gif[/img]


Again, these are the basic ways to use each Core, with more strategies and customization of the behaviour to come!

As always, give the demo a go and give me some more feedback if you can!

Cheers,
Chris

notes.title: A bit on how Core Lords works 2# - Controlling Elemental Cores!
notes.content:
[h2]The Core Types[/h2]

The “Cores” in Core Lords are concentrated elemental energy focused and controlled by you. There are 4 types of Cores: [b]Stonecores, Windcores, Watercores and Flamecores.[/b]

[th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/7f698f3de738d914693923943b6d545a10d6addc.gif[/img][/th]
[th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/42f294e9d27a80a6c9bc636da76302cf62382d07.gif[/img][/th]
[th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/a759553154b7546d90c6188b3c3a98fd55698260.gif[/img][/th]
[th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/820be0a57a7a83bcc888eb1b9f556afc482302d0.gif[/img][/th]

[h2]Summoning and Selecting[/h2]

Cores are summoned or controlled from the world. 
[list]
[*] Stonecores are specifically sized pieces of stone that can be selected and moved, dropped, pulled from the ground etc. 
[*] Watercores and Flamecores and summoned from water and flame sources, such as rivers and lava pools. 
[*] Windcores are easily accessed from environments with air to spin up.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/b5b64d4457606aa8b3386a5cf0730ce0e30eb026.gif[/img]


[h2]Movement and Action Points[/h2]

In the Action State (and Combat), cores can be moved with action points, both horizontally and vertically. Summoning will, in most cases, cost action points too. Cores can often be destroyed early to refund action points. 

As long as you have action points, you can transform the world to your goals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/815ee0c679d2cb60957871dacbcf02972f2189a2.gif[/img]


[h2]Unleash![/h2]

On leaving the Action State or ending a turn in combat, the Cores that are suspended by player control will trigger - dropping, falling, pushing, exploding - all sorts of things you can experiment with!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/c0b31a92df5930e788b3e77c1f45abed0ebc7141.gif[/img]

All sorts of interactions can happen, with the Cores being used to explore, solve puzzles, clear obstacles and battle enemies and bosses! (more detail on these in the next article)


[b]Next up:[/b]
[h2]Cores Interaction![/h2]
Here we will go into more detail on the Cores and how the they interact with each other.

In the meantime, give the demo a go and give me some feedback if you can!

Cheers,
Chris

notes.title: A bit on how Core Lords works 1# - Movement and States
notes.content:
Hello hello! I will be doing some updates and posts about how the game works. First up is Movement and States:

[h2]States[/h2]

Core Lords has two states, Exploration and Action. When in Exploration, movement is done through real-time navigation. But at almost any time you can jump into Action, which moves into a turn-based mode. Combat is done in the Action state as you might have guessed. 


[h2]Action Points[/h2]

Core Lords uses a shared Action Point system for ALL actions, including Action Movement. It does not use a separate “movement” resource.

Move one step, use one action point! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/b72deb5df5db0dd04d5d0f413271e57c1d74a183.gif[/img]


[h2]Movement[/h2]

Core Lords uses the usual horizontal planes but also emphasizes verticality of levels to battle and solve puzzles. The arena you are fighting in will shift and change as rocks fall and form, buildings crumble and dangerous elements block your path.

Because of this, you are able to make some jumps across gaps and drop down jumps. Nothing crazy here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/3df6ad14a7a24c4b4f1201ee2fb64e03a8c33587.gif[/img]

You can also suspend Stonecores (blocks of stone) using your powers to make temporary or semi-permanent paths as well, but more on that later.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/0474b80202d2a994c49bb3327c66aa3ce7f1e084.gif[/img]


[b]Next up:[/b] 
[h3]Controlling Elemental Cores![/h3]
Here we will go into the meat of the game: The Elemental Cores! 

In the meantime, give the demo a go and give me some feedback if you can!

Cheers,
Chris

notes.title: DEMO OUT NOW!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/6c15773edd374c534034264912c5b219f97c6aa8.png[/img]

The Core Lords Demo is now playable for everyone - [b]PLAY IT FREE NOW![/b] :D

All you need to do is to go to the game's Steam page and press the green button "Download Core Lords Demo" to start playing.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2357850/Core_Lords/

Remember to add the game to your wishlist as well!

I’m so excited for you to experience Core Lords and it would help greatly if you could share your first impressions of the Demo on all community and social media channels that you are active on with a link to the Steam page.

Also, tell your friends and family about it and get them to play the demo, talk about Core Lords and mention it everywhere you can. Thank you for any support!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43869109/20d05fc8a566989d993900554259302a7a570564.gif[/img]

[h3][b]WHAT TO EXPECT FROM THE DEMO[/b][/h3]

The demo will give a taste of the game, having a short intro to the story, world and mechanics. Roughly 30-40 minutes of play.

You will also be able to jump into quick battles where you can play around with 2 out of the 4 Core powers that will be available in the game (Stone/Wind), so you can get a feel for the battle mechanics, more powerful enemies and the destructible world.

Heads up: The game is still fresh and will have bugs and missing quality-of-life features.


[h3][b]DEMO FEEDBACK AND BUG REPORTING[/b][/h3]

Heading over to the discord to report any bugs or give feedback would be greatly appreciated! I will be around in Discord to answer questions as much as I can.

[b][url=http://discord.gg/XZX3PEBqQD]DISCORD[/url][/b]

Thanks again and I hope to hear from you all soon!

Cheers,
Chris
